metadata.description: A marketplace of self-owned, openly licensed Agent Skills for working with Bitcoin — the software, the protocol, and the money.

plugins.name: bitcoin-install
plugins.description: Install and first-run Bitcoin Core on macOS: the Homebrew formula (command-line tools) versus the cask (Qt desktop node), which one gives you what, and how to run a throwaway regtest network with Polar and Docker.

plugins.name: bitcoin-cli
plugins.description: Drive a Bitcoin Core node from the command line: bitcoin-cli flags and network selection, argument quoting, reading output and exit codes, BTC-vs-satoshi units and fee math, and the regtest workflow.

plugins.name: bitcoin-api
plugins.description: Talk to a Bitcoin Core node over its own network interfaces: JSON-RPC over HTTP, the unauthenticated REST interface, and ZMQ notifications — authentication, endpoints, parameters, batching, and error codes.

plugins.name: money
plugins.description: What money actually is: the properties that make something money, the functions it serves, and how to evaluate a monetary good against them.

plugins.name: bitcoin-code
plugins.description: Research the Bitcoin implementation and its specifications: locate consensus and policy rules in the bitcoin/bitcoin source with file:line evidence, trace when and why they changed, follow pull requests and review history, and map BIPs to the code that implements them.
